title: Secondary Headaches: IIH and Medication-Overuse Headache

steps.tx: A secondary headache syndrome characterised by elevated intracranial pressure in the absence of an intracranial mass lesion, hydrocephalus, or dural venous thrombosis is **idiopathic intracranial hypertension** (IIH, pseudotumor cerebri). Occurring predominantly in obese women of childbearing age, patients present with diffuse daily headaches, bilateral papilloedema, transient visual obscurations, and pulsatile tinnitus.
steps.say: A secondary headache syndrome characterized by elevated intracranial pressure without a mass, hydrocephalus, or venous thrombosis is idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Occurring predominantly in obese women of childbearing age, patients present with daily headaches, papilloedema, transient visual obscurations, and pulsatile tinnitus.

steps.tx: Diagnostic confirmation of IIH requires fulfilling the modified Dandy criteria: signs of raised intracranial pressure, normal neurological examination except for sixth cranial nerve palsy, normal brain parenchyma and venous sinuses on MRI/MRV, and documented elevated lumbar puncture opening pressure exceeding twenty-five centimetres of water with normal **cerebrospinal** fluid cytochemistry.
steps.say: Diagnostic confirmation of IIH requires fulfilling the modified Dandy criteria: signs of raised pressure, normal neurological exam except for sixth nerve palsy, normal MRI and MR venography, and documented lumbar puncture opening pressure exceeding twenty-five centimetres of water with normal CSF fluid.

nodes.label: Opening Pressure > 25 cm H2O Confirms IIH

steps.tx: The definitive first-line pharmacological treatment for idiopathic intracranial hypertension is the oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitor **acetazolamide**. By inhibiting carbonic anhydrase within choroid plexus epithelial cells, acetazolamide reduces cerebrospinal fluid production by up to fifty percent, successfully lowering intracranial pressure, relieving headache, and protecting against permanent optic atrophy and visual field loss.

By inhibiting carbonic anhydrase within choroid plexus epithelial cells, acetazolamide reduces CSF production by half, protecting against permanent optic atrophy.

steps.tx: Frequent, excessive consumption of acute abortive analgesics in patients with primary headaches paradoxically transforms episodic headaches into a chronic daily headache pattern termed **medication overuse headache** (MOH). Defined as headache occurring on fifteen or more days per month in a patient taking simple analgesics for fifteen days/month or triptans/opioids for ten days/month, definitive cure requires structured withdrawal of the overused agent.
steps.say: Frequent excessive consumption of acute analgesics in primary headache patients paradoxically transforms headaches into a chronic daily pattern termed medication overuse headache. Occurring fifteen or more days monthly from overused analgesics or triptans, definitive cure requires complete withdrawal of the offending medication.

steps.tx: Persistent leakage of cerebrospinal fluid through a dural puncture defect into the epidural space causes low intracranial CSF pressure and traction on pain-sensitive meninges, producing **post-dural puncture headache** (PDPH). The pathognomonic clinical feature is severe orthostatic (postural) headache that develops within fifteen minutes of sitting or standing upright and resolves completely upon lying flat.
steps.say: Persistent leakage of cerebrospinal fluid through a dural puncture defect causes low intracranial pressure and meningeal traction, producing post-dural puncture headache. The pathognomonic clinical feature is severe orthostatic headache that develops upon sitting or standing and resolves completely upon lying flat.

steps.tx: Conservative management of post-dural puncture headache comprises bed rest, aggressive oral or intravenous hydration, simple analgesics, and oral caffeine. For severe, disabling orthostatic headaches persisting beyond forty-eight hours, the definitive therapeutic gold standard is an autologous **epidural** blood patch, where fifteen to twenty millilitres of the patient's own blood is injected into the epidural space to seal the dural hole.

steps.tx: Clinical triage of acute headache requires rigorous screening for secondary life-threatening aetiologies using the SNOOP **mnemonic** (Systemic symptoms/fever, Neurological deficits, Onset sudden or thunderclap, Older age over fifty years, Pattern change or Papilloedema, Positional aggravation). Any red flag finding mandates emergency neuroimaging and vascular assessment.

steps.tx: The group of primary headaches defined by severe unilateral head pain linked with ipsilateral cranial parasympathetic autonomic activation comprises the trigeminal **autonomic** cephalalgias (TACs). In addition to cluster headache, this family includes paroxysmal hemicrania (which responds completely to indomethacin) and short-lasting unilateral neuralgiform headache attacks with conjunctival injection and tearing (SUNCT).
